content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
Context: during release v0.127.0 QA (2026-10-28), a real Composio GitHub event automation test on Agenta's staging stage showed three side problems in the event automations feature. Mahmoud (the owner) asked for separate sessions that each open a fix PR. This session handles only the repo field format. Two other sessions handle sending edited filters to Composio and a startup log of the registered webhook URL; do not touch those. Rules: work in your own worktree, no deploys, no merges. /m (web/mobile) is the main app. Plain English, no em dashes.

Task:
Fix: the event automation form accepts a GitHub repo filter that Composio cannot use.

Bug: when a user creates an event automation for a GitHub event, the filter form accepted `repo: agenta` with a separate `owner: agenta-ai`. Composio's trigger schema says `repo` must be in `owner/repo` form and ignores `owner` when `repo` is set, so the filter does nothing.

Do:
1. Find where the event filter form is built (web/mobile automations: `EventPickerPanel.tsx` under the automations feature, and the filter fields that come from the Composio event schema) and where the API accepts `trigger_config` for subscriptions (`api/oss/src/core/triggers/`, `api/oss/src/apis/fastapi/triggers/`). Check Composio's schema text for the field.
2. Choose the smallest correct fix, preferably one place: normalize on the frontend if the user typed only the repo name and an owner field exists (join to `owner/repo`), or show a clear inline hint and block "Done" until the value has the `owner/repo` form. Do not invent new UI text beyond one short hint; quote any new user-facing string in the PR body for Mahmoud's approval. If the API should also reject a bad value, return a 422 with a plain message.
3. Tests for the normalization or validation. Run `pnpm lint-fix` in `web/` for frontend changes, and ruff for API changes (`~/.local/bin/ruff`).
4. Open a PR into `main` titled `fix(frontend): require owner/repo for GitHub event filters` (or `fix(api)` if the fix is in the API). Body per the write-pr-description skill. Ready for review. Never merge.
Done: PR open with tests passing, link reported, new strings listed.

# Write PR Descriptions

Write PRs that a teammate can understand at a glance. Lead with what was broken from the user's point of view, then show the fix in plain words with a concrete before/after. No padding, no checkbox theater, no jargon-first openings.

This is the default quality bar from the first draft. Don't ship a generic version expecting to fix it after feedback.

## 0. The prefilled template

GitHub prefills every PR from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, which asks for Summary, Testing, Demo, Checklist, and Contributor Resources. That is not what this repo's PRs look like. Replace the prefilled body with the structure in section 2.

Two parts of the template still apply:

- **Demo.** UI changes need a capture from the real app running your branch. Never substitute a mock-up, a component harness, or a recreated screen. If you cannot run the app, say the demo is outstanding and why, rather than filling the space with something that proves nothing.
- **Testing.** Keep the substance under a `## Tests` heading. You do not need the template's three subheadings unless the change is large enough that they help.

Drop the Checklist and Contributor Resources if the author is a core maintainer of the repo. They exist for first-time outside contributors and the team does not fill them in.

## 1. Title

The title states the actual change in plain words.

- Use the conventional prefix the repo already uses, e.g. `[fix] <Title>`, `[feat] <Title>`, `[chore] <Title>`, `[docs] <Title>`.
- If the user gave you an issue id, suffix it: `[fix] <Title> [AGE-1234]`.
- Define the title as an active intent in present tense, e.g `[fix] Resolve broken evaluation links`.
- Keep it under ~70 characters. Detail goes in the body.

Good vs bad:

- Good: `[fix] Map OpenInference tool definitions into real tool objects`
- Bad: `fix(api) parse X into structured objects` (abstract, says nothing concrete)
- Bad: `Update tool handling` (vague, no symptom, no domain)

## 2. Body structure

Use this shape unless the change is truly trivial:

```
## Context
<one or two sentences: the symptom a user or teammate would notice, then the root cause in plain words>

## Changes
<plain-words explanation of the change, with a concrete before/after when a data shape, signature, or behavior changed>

## Tests / notes
<short bullet list or prose: what you verified, anything reviewers should watch for>

## What to QA
<only for user-visible changes: short steps for the manual tester, see section 7>
```

Adapt the headings if the situation calls for it (e.g. a pure feature PR might use "What this adds" instead of "What was broken"). The order stays the same: the obeservation (symptom or user-visible change first or intent), then the changes, then verification and validation.

## 3. Show, don't restate the diff

When a transformation changed a data shape, signature, or behavior, show it concretely.

Good:

> Tool definitions coming from OpenInference traces arrived as
>
> ```
> [{tool: {json_schema: "..."}}]
> ```
>
> The playground expected
>
> ```
> [{type: "function", function: {...}}]
> ```
>
> So the parser now unwraps `json_schema` and rebuilds each entry in the expected shape before handing it to the playground.

Bad:

> - Updated tool parsing logic
> - Improved data handling
> - Added support for OpenInference tools

The second version restates the diff in vague bullets. It tells the reader nothing the file list doesn't.

## 4. Cut the padding

Things to remove before you publish:

- Generic "Summary" or "Overview" sections that paraphrase the title.
- Checkbox theater ("- [x] code written - [x] tested") unless the repo's template requires it.
- Bullet lists that restate every changed file. The diff already shows that.
- Marketing words: "comprehensive", "robust", "seamlessly", "leverage", "powerful".
- Bullets that exist only to fill space. Prefer one clear sentence to three vague bullets.

## 5. Prose rules

Apply these general writing rules:

- **No em dashes.** Replace with a period and a new sentence, parentheses, or a semicolon. Absolute rule.
- Active voice.
- Short sentences by default. Longer ones only when they help the flow.
- Complete sentences. Snippets are fine when they keep things short and clear.
- Don't overuse bold or bullets. Use them when they aid quick reading. Otherwise prose.
- 11th-grade English, except for unavoidable technical terms.

## 6. Tests / notes section

Keep this section short and concrete. Useful contents:

- What you ran locally (`pnpm test`, `pytest tests/...`, manual UI check on `/observability`).
- Anything reviewers should poke at (a known-fragile area, a follow-up not in this PR).
- Migration or rollout notes if relevant.

Skip the section entirely if there is nothing real to say. A blank "Tests" heading is worse than no heading.

## 7. What to QA section

If the change is user-visible and a teammate will test it manually, add a "What to QA" section. Write it for a tester who knows the product and has context: skip the basics, point at the right screens, and state the expected result of every check.

- One line per check: where to go, what to do, what they should see.
- Name the exact pages and flows. "Test the feature" is not a check.
- Include the regression to watch for: the thing this change is most likely to have broken.
- If a check needs setup (a seeded project, an older record, a feature flag), say so in the same line.
- Use simple, clear language. Same prose rules as section 5.

Example:

> ## What to QA
> - Create a new automatic evaluator, name it, save. The table shows your name with a v1 tag, not "default".
> - Edit it and commit a config change. The name stays, the version bumps to v2.
> - Regression: run a new evaluation. The variant chips still say "default", not the app name.

Skip the section when nothing is user-visible (pure refactor, CI, docs). A reviewer-only change needs the Tests section, not this one.

## 8. Reviewer's first-30-seconds test

Before you finalize, read your own draft and ask:

1. After 30 seconds, does a reviewer know **the context** and **what changed**?
2. Is there a concrete before/after anywhere a shape or behavior moved?
3. Did you delete every sentence that doesn't earn its place?
4. Did you scan for em dashes and marketing words?

If any answer is no, edit before you push.

## 9. Worked example

A bad first draft:

```
## Summary
- Updated the tool parsing logic to handle OpenInference traces
- Improved compatibility with the playground
- Added robust error handling for edge cases

## Includes
- Modified parseTools function
- Updated type definitions
- Added new test cases
```

A good rewrite:

```
## Context
When you opened an OpenInference trace in the playground, the tools panel was empty. The trace stored tool definitions as `[{tool: {json_schema: "..."}}]`, but the playground expected the OpenAI shape `[{type: "function", function: {...}}]`, so the parser dropped them silently.

## Changes
`parseToolsFromTrace` now unwraps `json_schema` and rebuilds each entry in the OpenAI shape before it hits the playground. Traces that already use the OpenAI shape pass through unchanged.

Before:
[{tool: {json_schema: "{\"name\": \"get_weather\", ...}"}}]

After:
[{type: "function", function: {name: "get_weather", parameters: {...}}}]

## Tests
- Added a unit test in parseToolsFromTrace.test.ts covering both shapes.
- Opened a real OpenInference trace from the staging project and confirmed the tools panel renders.

## What to QA
- Open an OpenInference trace in the playground (the staging project has them). The tools panel lists the tools.
- Regression: open a trace from the OpenAI SDK. The tools panel still renders as before.
```

The second version is cleaner and tells the reviewer everything they need to start reading the diff.

I opened [Agenta-AI/agenta#7878](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/pull/7878) into `main`. It is ready for review and not merged. Commit `baedcbb1d9`.

**The task assumed a rule that is wrong for most GitHub triggers.** I read the schemas of all 46 GitHub triggers in Composio's catalog:
- 45 of them want `owner` plus a bare repo name, for example `repo: agenta`.
- Only `GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_CREATED` wants `repo` in `owner/repo` form. The schema says "Must be in 'owner/repo' format". This trigger ignores `owner` when `repo` is set. The staging test used this trigger.

So I did not add a rule that always requires `owner/repo`. That rule would break the other 45 triggers. I also changed the PR title, because the requested title, "require owner/repo for GitHub event filters", says the opposite of what the code does. The PR title is `fix(frontend): join a bare repo name with its owner for GitHub event filters`.

**The fix:** When the user clicks Done in the event picker, the picker joins a bare repo name with the owner, so `repo: agenta` with `owner: agenta-ai` becomes `repo: agenta-ai/agenta`. It does this only when the field's schema description asks for `owner/repo` format. Other triggers send their filters unchanged.
- The helper is `normalizeRepoFilters` in `@agenta/entities/gatewayTrigger`.
- `EventPickerPanel.tsx` calls it on Done.

**New user-facing strings:** none. There is no API change.

**Checks:**
- 7 new unit tests pass. They use trimmed copies of the real Composio schemas.
- `tsc`, eslint and `pnpm lint-fix` pass.
- CI is still running.

**Not done:**
- I did not check the change on `/m`, because this session does not deploy.
- One case stays open. On `GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_CREATED`, if the user types only `repo: agenta` and no owner, the value is still sent as typed. To block that, the form needs a new inline hint. That needs Mahmoud's approval for new UI text, so I left it out. The PR body says this.

# Release merge queue

Mahmoud says "add <PR> to the merge queue", or hands over the "In" list from the
`release-dashboard` skill. The goal is speed without losing quality, so every PR gets its own
agent and all agents run at the same time. A coordinator (the orchestrator) keeps one note with the
queue state and the merge order.

## Coordinator

1. **Permission check, once, at the start.** Check that this session has Mahmoud's word that you
   may merge into the release branch. If it does not, ask once, before any agent starts, and list
   every other permission the run needs in the same ask.
2. **Queue note.** Keep `~/agenta-release-<version>/queue.md` with one row per PR: PR, owner
   agent, state (`reading`, `fixing`, `waiting CI`, `ready`, `merged`, `blocked`), merge SHA, and
   notes. Add a "Merge order" section for dependencies, for example "#7801 and #7802 must merge
   together" or "#7810 after #7798 (same migration chain)". Agents write only their own row.
3. **Start one agent per PR, all at once.** Give each agent this skill, the PR number, the release
   branch, the release PR number and the queue note path. Mahmoud's dashboard comment for the PR
   goes in the brief too.
4. **Release branch CI.** The release branch runs CI once for the batch. When a check goes red
   there, start one agent for a quick fix PR into the release branch.

## Hard rules for each PR agent

- Load `~/.claude/skills/plain-writing/SKILL.md` before you write any PR text, commit message,
  GitHub comment, issue, release PR line or report, and follow it.
- **Merge target is the release branch only. NEVER merge into `main`.** Check
  `gh pr view N --json baseRefName` right before the merge. Retarget with
  `gh api -X PATCH repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/pulls/N -f base=<release-branch>` (`gh pr edit` is
  broken here).
- Merge with `gh pr merge N --merge --admin`. Always a merge commit, never `--squash`. Admin is
  needed because the branch policy blocks self-approval. No `--delete-branch`.
- **Clones only.** Never use GitButler and never run `git worktree` in `~/code/agenta` (Mahmoud's
  workspace). Never write in `~/code/agenta`. Work in your own clone:
  `git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git ~/code/agenta-mq-<PR>`.
  Raw git is fine in that clone.
- **Clean up when you finish, merged or not.** Delete the clone, stop and remove every docker
  container and volume you started (by exact name, never by pattern), and remove your temp files.
  Disk space is a recurring problem on the dev box.
- **Conflicts.** Merge the release branch into the PR branch, resolve the conflicts, and push
  normally. Never rebase and never force push. Do not touch a PR that only waits for CI, because a
  push restarts its CI. For a fork with `maintainerCanModify` false, do not push. Report the
  conflict instead. Fork CI may wait for approval:
  `gh api -X POST repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/actions/runs/<id>/approve`.
- Every GitHub comment starts with `🤖 _The AI agent says:_ `. Never sign as Claude. Exception: bot
  commands that must be the exact body (for example `/preview`).
- No stage or production deploys, no agenta_cloud workflows, no snapshot builds.
- The agenta repo is PUBLIC. Never put customer data in a PR, commit, issue or comment: no Stripe
  ids (`sub_`, `in_`, `cus_`, `evt_`, `pi_`), no payment or plan history of a named or id-prefixed
  customer, no emails or names, no cloud hosts, project ids or IPs. Keep such evidence in the
  private notes folder and write "details are in the private release notes" on GitHub. An edit
  does not fix a leak (GitHub keeps the edit history), so delete the comment and post a clean one.
- Ruff: `~/.local/bin/ruff` (never `uvx ruff`). Frontend: `pnpm lint-fix` in `web/`. Lockfiles: the
  pinned tools (web pnpm 11.x reads overrides only from `web/pnpm-workspace.yaml`;
  `services/runner` and `docs/` use pnpm 10 and read the `pnpm` field in `package.json`; uv 0.11.14
  for Python locks).
- A sandbox image change (`services/runner/images/sandbox/**`, `agent-requirements.txt`, harness
  pins) must bump `services/runner/config/sandbox-recipe.json` in the same PR.
- Keep notes under `~/agenta-release-<version>/`, never `/tmp`. Write `<PR>.md` there and keep your
  row in `queue.md` current.

## Steps for each PR agent

**Ship record first.** Before step 0, read the newest PR comment with
`<!-- ship-record: head=<sha> -->` (written by the `pr-ready` skill) and compare its head with
`gh pr view N --json headRefOid`. Skip every step whose gate the record shows as passed for the
current head (review loops, QA, CodeRabbit, CI), and use its links in your report and in the
release PR lines. Run only the gates it marks as left to the merge queue, the gates it does not
list, and the gates that commits after its head affect.

0. **Labels first.** "Add to merge queue" means Mahmoud approved the PR. Remove every review-request
   label (`needs-review`, `need review`, `ai-review`, `implementing`, and any other label that asks
   for review or says work is in progress), then add `lgtm` and `merge queue`. If `gh pr edit`
   fails, use `gh api -X DELETE repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/issues/N/labels/<name>` and
   `gh api repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/issues/N/labels -f "labels[]=lgtm" -f "labels[]=merge queue"`.
   After the merge, remove `merge queue` and keep `lgtm`. If you stop without merging, keep
   `merge queue` and say why in the report.
1. **Read the PR.** Title, body, linked issue, diff, files, base. Retarget it if the base is not
   the release branch. Check that the change is not already on the release branch and not
   superseded by another PR. If it is, stop and report.
   **Owner PRs (author `mmabrouk`):** read the body and comments for what was already reviewed and
   QA'd, what is left to check, and any deploy steps. Copy those into the release PR body (step 9)
   and your notes, so nothing gets lost.
2. **Read every CodeRabbit item.** Review bodies (including folded "outside diff" and nitpick
   sections), inline threads, and issue comments: `gh api repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/pulls/N/reviews`,
   `.../pulls/N/comments`, `.../issues/N/comments`. If CodeRabbit has not reviewed the current head,
   or skipped it because of the base, comment `@coderabbitai review` and wait for it.
3. **Decide each finding.** Fix it when it is a real problem. When you do not fix it, reply in the
   thread with a short reason. Never drop one silently.
4. **Review.**
   - If the PR has a review-loop record for its current head (a comment with
     `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> -->`), do not review again. Read the record and use it.
   - An owner PR that the body shows was reviewed extensively skips the extra review.
   - An external or quick PR without a record runs the `review-loop` skill. A quick PR gets one
     round.
   - In every case, check the points the loop does not cover: /m (`web/mobile`) is the main app and
     /w (`web/oss`) is the old classic app, so a user-facing change that only reaches /w is a gap
     to report. Quote any new user-facing string in your report (no invented user copy). Run the
     tests for the area you touched.
5. **Resolve all threads.** After your fix or reply, resolve every review thread (CodeRabbit and
   human) with the GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation. List threads with
   `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"Agenta-AI",name:"agenta"){pullRequest(number:N){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved comments(first:1){nodes{author{login} body}}}}}}}'`.
   A human reviewer's request that you cannot settle yourself is a question for Mahmoud, not a
   resolve.
6. **Checks, by change type.**
   - Docs-only or test-only change: merge at once.
   - Frontend-only change: wait only for the web image builds (`agenta-web`, `agenta-web-mobile`).
   - Any other change: wait for lint, format, types, CodeQL, gitleaks, migration gate, image
     builds, and the api / sdk / services / runner test jobs (unit, integration, acceptance),
     including the Railway preview test jobs. Merging closes the PR and cancels running jobs, so
     do not merge before these finish.
   - Never wait for web test jobs: anything with "web" in the name that is a test, Storybook,
     Playwright. Also ignore the CLA check, `cleanup / mutate` and Vercel (the old classic app).
   - A red required check: find the cause and fix it, or prove it is also red on the release tip.
     "Build and deploy preview" (the marketing website) failing for infra reasons with no
     `web/website` change: record the evidence and go on.
   - Do not poll in a tight loop. Sleep in Bash between checks.
7. **Merge first, fix forward.** When a head passed CI and your follow-up change is one or two
   lines (a lint fix or a nit), push it and merge without waiting for a new CI run. The release
   branch runs CI once for the batch, and a red check there gets a quick fix PR. Never do this for
   migrations, auth, the runner or credentials. Those wait for full CI on the final head.
8. **Merge** into the release branch (rule above). Record the merge commit SHA in your notes and in
   `queue.md`. Then remove the `merge queue` label and keep `lgtm`. Follow the merge order in
   `queue.md`: a PR that must merge with another one waits until both are `ready`.
9. **Close the linked issue.** A merge into a release branch does not close issues. For each issue
   the PR fixes ("Fixes/Closes #N" in the body, or named in the title like `[7505]`), close it:
   `gh issue close N --comment "🤖 _The AI agent says:_ Fixed by #PR, merged into <release-branch> (<sha>). It ships with <version>."`.
   If the PR only partly fixes the issue, comment instead and say what is left.
10. **Release PR body: Final QA and Deploy steps.** Read the body with
    `gh api repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/pulls/<release-PR> -q .body`. STOP if it is empty or does not
    start with "New version", because writing it back would wipe the release body. Re-read right
    before you write, because other agents edit it too. Append, never overwrite, and write back with
    `gh api -X PATCH repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/pulls/<release-PR> -F body=@file`. Read it again after
    the write and check the original text is still there.
    - Under `## Final QA`, add `- [ ] #PR <what to check, how, and what a pass looks like>` for
      behavior CI cannot prove (load, concurrency, real providers, real sandboxes, UI flows in /m,
      migrations on real data, anything a review flagged as untested). For owner PRs, copy the
      "left to check" items from the PR body here. Skip this when CI is enough proof, and say so.
    - Under `## Deploy steps`, add `- [ ] #PR <what to run, when, on which stages>; see the PR for details`
      for anything that runs at deploy time (a one-time script, a data backfill, an env var or
      values change, a manual step in a provider dashboard). Do not run it against a real database
      or stage. Prove it on a throwaway local database, check it is safe to run twice, and write
      the exact procedure in the notes folder and the PR body.
11. **Clean up** (hard rule above), then **report** in short plain sentences, and write the same to
    `<PR>.md`: merged or not, merge SHA, what CodeRabbit raised and what you did, which review ran
    (record reused, loop rounds, or skipped and why), what you fixed, any check you did not wait
    for and why, the issue you closed, the Final QA and Deploy steps lines you added, and any risk
    or question for Mahmoud.
